vendor: Aider AI / Paul Gauthier — pip package `aider-chat` (Apache-2.0), repo Aider-AI/aider
surfaces: CLI (interactive TUI + `--message`/`--message-file` one-shot), optional Streamlit web UI (`aider --gui`), pip-installed console script. No upstream VS Code/JetBrains extension, so no IDE globalStorage/state.vscdb path applies. Windows binary is the pip console script `aider.exe` (already matched by Discodex `Provider::from_executable("aider")` at src/provider.rs:190). Aider is NOT cloud-only: it is a local CLI, and its transcript is written locally.
binaries: `pip install aider-chat` → console script `aider` (Windows: `aider.exe`); upstream pyproject.toml: `name = "aider-chat"`, `[project.scripts] aider = "aider.main:main"`

paths: DEFAULT: <git working-tree root>\.aider.chat.history.md  (e.g. C:\Users\PC\Documents\MyRepo\.aider.chat.history.md) — NOT under %USERPROFILE% by default (aider/args.py:274-276: os.path.join(git_root, ".aider.chat.history.md") if git_root else ".aider.chat.history.md"; git_root from aider/main.py:60-66 git.Repo(search_parent_directories=True).working_tree_dir)
<git working-tree root>\.aider.input.history  (user prompt history only — a privacy trap, must never be read)

%USERPROFILE%\.aider.chat.history.md  — only if the user sets AIDER_CHAT_HISTORY_FILE=... or --chat-history-file=... (args.py:41 auto_env_var_prefix="AIDER_"; aider/website/docs/config/dotenv.md:178-179). NOT a default location.

%USERPROFILE%\.aider.conf.yml and %USERPROFILE%\.aider.model.settings.yml / .aider.model.metadata.json (config/metadata; home is in the search path per aider/main.py:305-312 — no activity content; whether the settings file is auto-written by a normal run is UNVERIFIED)
opt-in: --llm-history-file <path> (plain text 'ROLE ISO-8601\ncontent' blocks, default None) and --analytics-log <path> (JSONL analytics, default None)

NO per-project/per-session subdirectory layout — the transcript file sits directly in the repo root and holds every session for that repo appended together. Contrast: Codex/Claude Code/Antigravity use per-session directories.
storage.format: Plain UTF-8 Markdown transcript (human-oriented, NOT JSON/JSONL). Record types are line-shaped, so Discodex's existing line-based tailer/parse_line_for contract fits: '# aider chat started at YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' = session header; '#### <user prompt>' = user turn; '> <text>' = tool/console output (blockquote); anything else = assistant reply text. Canonical structure is defined by aider/utils.py:148-194 (split_chat_history_markdown): '# ' = header, '> ' = tool role, '#### ' = user role, rest = assistant role.
storage.append_semantics: APPEND-ONLY and LIVE. aider/io.py:1128-1132 opens the file with mode "a" on every append and never rewrites it; /clear only clears in-memory messages (aider/commands.py:411-437). The file grows forever, is never rotated or truncated, and holds many sessions concatenated. Aider re-execs itself when it guessed the wrong git root (aider/main.py:713-720, 'Recursing with correct repo'), which can emit two session headers, possibly into two different files.
storage.session_file_naming: Fixed name '.aider.chat.history.md' in the git working-tree root (aider/args.py:274-276); overridable via --chat-history-file / AIDER_CHAT_HISTORY_FILE. Companion file '.aider.input.history' (aider/args.py:271-273). Session/thread ID: NONE — sessions are delimited only by the '# aider chat started at' header inside the same file; project grouping = the repo folder name (i.e. the parent folder of the transcript file).

fields.project: Recoverable. The transcript's own path gives the git working-tree root; publish only its final folder name (Discodex policy). Corroborated in-band by the banner line '> Git repo: .git with 300 files' (aider/coders/base_coder.py:251-262).
fields.model: Recoverable. Startup banner '> Main model: <model> with <edit_format> edit format' plus optional '> Weak model: <model>' / '> Editor model: ...' (aider/coders/base_coder.py:207-248), emitted through io.tool_output via coder.show_announcements() (aider/main.py:1042 → aider/coders/base_coder.py:550-554) so it lands in the transcript. Re-emitted on /model switch (aider/main.py:1179-1180). Legacy format (<= v0.47): '> Models: <main> with <fmt> edit format, weak model <weak>' (seen 523x in the upstream fixture) — format churn already observed.
fields.file_basename: Recoverable, repo-relative path: '> Applied edit to <path>' (aider/coders/base_coder.py:2330-2334), '> Did not apply edit to <path> (--dry-run)' (2332), '> Committing <path> before applying edits.' (2188), '> Added <path> to the chat.' (283-287). Only the basename may be published; the repo-relative path must be truncated to the file name.
fields.tool_activity: Partially recoverable from English console lines, not from structured tool records: '> Applied edit to X' (edit), '> Running <shell command>' (aider/coders/base_coder.py:2472 — the raw command MUST be dropped, only a fixed label published), '> Committing X before applying edits.', '> Commit <sha> <msg>' (aider/repo.py:313), '> Tokens: N sent, M received. Cost: ...' (aider/coders/base_coder.py:2023, 2102-2109 — emitted once per LLM response = reliable turn boundary). With function-call coders the tool-call arguments JSON is dumped verbatim into the transcript (aider/coders/base_coder.py:1830-1834, 'self.io.ai_output(json.dumps(args, indent=4))') — that blob can contain full file contents and must be ignored entirely.
fields.phase: Approximate only. '#### ' = new user turn → Thinking; '> ...' tool line → RunningTools; '> Tokens: ...' = LLM turn finished → back to Thinking. There is no explicit phase field and no structured tool/phase records.
fields.timestamps: Only the session header is timestamped: '# aider chat started at YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' (aider/io.py:335-336, datetime.now().strftime) — LOCAL wall clock, NO timezone, 1-second resolution. Every other line is untimestamped; ordering is file order only, so per-turn timing must use the observation time.

parser_strategy:
Line-oriented, so it fits Discodex's existing parse_line_for(provider, line) contract with NO change to the tailer (the file is newline-delimited and append-only). Map (after trimming trailing "  " markdown hard-break spaces):

1. "# aider chat started at YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" → ParsedEvent::SessionMetadata{project: <final folder name of the transcript's parent dir>, cwd: <repo root>} + ParsedEvent::TaskStarted{started_at_ms: naive local time parsed with chrono → Local offset}. This line also acts as the session boundary: it must reset the previous session's current_file/language for that path (all sessions share one file).
2. "#### <text>" → ParsedEvent::TaskStarted{started_at_ms: observation time} (new user turn = new task, gives the per-turn elapsed timer). The prompt text after the marker is NEVER read into any event.
3. "> Main model: <model> with <format> edit format" or "> Model: <model> ..." → ParsedEvent::AgentDetected{agent: <model id>} after sanitising to [A-Za-z0-9._:/-] and ≤128 chars (mirror deepseek_model_label). "> Models: <main> with <fmt> edit format, weak model <weak>" (legacy) → same, taking the first model.
4. "> Weak model: ..." / "> Editor model: ..." → ignored (only the main model is published).
5. "> Applied edit to <path>" → ParsedEvent::ToolStarted{activity: ToolActivity{label: "Editing files", file: basename(<path>), language: language_from_file(basename)}} immediately followed by ParsedEvent::ToolFinished (aider's edit is synchronous). "> Did not apply edit to <path> (--dry-run)" → ignore.
6. "> Committing <path> before applying edits." → ToolStarted{ToolActivity{label: "Editing files", file: basename, language}} + ToolFinished.
7. "> Added <path> to the chat." → ToolStarted{ToolActivity{label: "Reading project files", file: basename, language}} + ToolFinished.
8. "> Running <command>" → ToolStarted{ToolActivity{label: classify_tool("run", <command>) (fixed label only), file: None, language: None}} + ToolFinished. The command string itself must be dropped inside the parser (never stored, never published). Note classify_tool() already reduces it to a constant like "Running command"/"Running Rust tests".
9. "> Tokens: ..." → ParsedEvent::ToolFinished (+ optional Thinking{reasoning: None}) — marks the end of one LLM turn.
10. "> Commit <sha> <msg>" → ToolFinished only (a commit is not task completion).
11. Everything else (assistant prose, diff bodies, JSON tool-arg blobs) → NO event. Unmatched lines are dropped wholesale, which is the core privacy guarantee: the parser is an allow-list, never a pass-through.
Phase/activity therefore become: Thinking on '####' and after '> Tokens:', RunningTools while a '> ' tool line is active.
discodex_plan:
PROVIDER: reuse the existing `Provider::Aider` variant (src/provider.rs:18,95,125) — no new variant; keep display_name "Aider".

SESSION ROOT (the hard part): the default transcript is NOT under %USERPROFILE%, so session_sources() (src/provider.rs:348-371, home-rooted) cannot find it. Three-tier plan:
 (T1, zero-risk, immediate) Add SessionSource{provider: Aider, root: home.join(".aider.chat.history.md")} to catch users who set AIDER_CHAT_HISTORY_FILE=%USERPROFILE%\.aider.chat.history.md or --chat-history-file. Cheap, no regression.
 (T2, recommended) Config-driven roots: extend AppConfig (src/config.rs:9-26) with `aider_project_paths: Vec<PathBuf>` (serde default empty) and build one SessionSource per configured repo root. `session_sources()` gains `&AppConfig` (or a new `aider_sources(extra_roots)`), each root R = the repo root; the transcript sits directly in R.
 (T3, optional, phase 2) Auto-discovery: enumerate running `aider.exe` processes (CreateToolhelp32Snapshot), read each process CWD from the PEB (NtQueryInformationProcess → PEB.ProcessParameters → RTL_USER_PROCESS_PARAMETERS.CurrentDirectory.DosPath; x64 offsets PEB+0x20, params+0x38/0x40), walk up to the nearest .git to get the working-tree root, and add that root as a session source. This needs new unsafe Win32 code but no new crate (the `windows` crate already exposes the APIs); it is offset/architecture-fragile, so it must fail safe (any error → ignore, keep focused detection).

IS_SESSION_LOG (src/provider.rs:373-395): the current code early-returns false for any name not ending in ".jsonl", so the Aider branch must be evaluated BEFORE that check. Rule: `Provider::Aider => lower_filename == ".aider.chat.history.md"` (exact match, like Antigravity's "transcript.jsonl"). Deliberately EXCLUDE ".aider.input.history" — it stores raw user prompts and carries no activity signal (privacy hazard, zero value).

WATCHER (src/watcher.rs): NO change needed to LogTailer — the transcript is newline-delimited and append-only, so read_new()/the pending-line buffer already work, and no zstd path is required. recent_logs() also works unchanged (the file sits at depth 0 of the repo root; the '.'-dir skip rule is irrelevant). One addition: because a repo transcript can grow to hundreds of MB, the initial read must use read_from_start() only on a bounded prefix (or start at EOF and back-fill the last N KB), otherwise startup stalls.

MAIN (src/main.rs): (a) session_sources() must become dynamic — the worker has to re-resolve the Aider roots (config change or T3 discovery) and call watcher.watch(root, RecursiveMode::NonRecursive) for newly discovered roots; today the roots are computed once at line 193 and watched at lines 302-317. (b) has_session_tracking(): do NOT flip Aider to true as-is. foreground.rs:25,28 and main.rs:66,112 suppress the focused-window fallback for any provider with session tracking, so flipping it would DELETE today's working "focused Aider terminal" presence for every user whose repo is not discoverable. Introduce a separate capability flag (e.g. `Provider::session_optional()` or `session_backed`) so presence selection prefers a fresh session snapshot and falls back to the foreground snapshot when the session is absent/stale. This is the single most important main.rs/state.rs change.

risks: LOCATION (blocking): the default transcript lives in the git working-tree root of whatever repo aider was launched in — there is no home-level default and no per-project directory to scan. A home-rooted SessionSource finds nothing unless the user sets AIDER_CHAT_HISTORY_FILE; a default install therefore needs T2 (config-listed repo roots) or T3 (process-CWD discovery, new unsafe PEB code) before any Aider presence can appear.

PRIVACY (severe if mishandled): the transcript contains the user's prompts, the assistant's replies, full SEARCH/REPLACE diffs and, for function-call coders, raw tool-argument JSON including whole file contents. Any parser that forwards a line verbatim publishes prompts/secrets to Discord. Mitigation: strict literal-prefix allow-list, never emit unmatched content, drop shell command text, and keep the two privacy unit tests mandatory.

FORMAT CHURN: the transcript is user-facing English; aider already renamed '> Models:' to '> Main model:' (v0.47 -> current). Any prefix change silently degrades the adapter; mitigate with a legacy+current prefix table, unit test 5, and fail-safe (emit nothing rather than guess).

AMBIGUITY / FALSE POSITIVES: assistant prose can contain lines starting with '####' or '> ' (aider even quotes user text in replies), which can fake a user turn or a tool line. Restrict matches to the known prefixes plus the trailing '  ' hard-break marker, and prefer the '# aider chat started at' / '> Applied edit to ' shapes that cannot occur in prose without the marker.

TIME: only the session header carries a timestamp (local wall clock, no TZ, 1s resolution); per-turn elapsed time must come from observation time, so the timer is approximate and will drift from aider's internal clock.

ONE FILE, MANY SESSIONS, NO ROTATION: every session in a repo appends to the same file forever, so session state must be reset on each '# aider chat started at' header and startup must not read_from_start() a multi-hundred-MB transcript.

REGRESSION RISK in Discodex: flipping Provider::Aider.has_session_tracking() to true suppresses the focused-window fallback (src/foreground.rs:25,28; src/main.rs:66,112) and would remove Aider presence entirely for users whose repo path is not discoverable. Requires the session-vs-foreground merge described above.

REPO-PATH DERIVATION: the git root is derived by walking up for .git; worktrees/submodules (where .git is a file) and aider's own re-exec path can point the transcript at an unexpected directory — the project name shown must be the final folder name only.
SHELL COMMANDS: '> Running <cmd>' contains raw commands with paths/secrets; classify_tool() must be applied in-parse and the command string discarded, never stored in ActivityState.
confidence: HIGH on all storage/format facts: verified directly in upstream source at commit 5dc9490 (args.py, io.py, utils.py, base_coder.py, main.py, commands.py, analytics.py, models.py) plus a REAL upstream transcript fixture (tests/fixtures/chat-history.md) and live HTTP checks of the cited URLs and of the lobehub icon package. MEDIUM on the integration plan: the discovery mechanism (config-listed repo roots vs PEB process-CWD enumeration) is design, not fact, and the PEB offsets would need on-device verification on x64.
summary:
Aider is NOT cloud-only: it writes a local, live, append-only activity log — but not where one expects. The artifact is a human-facing Markdown transcript, `<git working-tree root>\.aider.chat.history.md` (upstream default, aider/args.py:274-276), NOT %USERPROFILE%\.aider.chat.history.md (home only if the user explicitly sets AIDER_CHAT_HISTORY_FILE/--chat-history-file). The .aider.input.history file next to it holds raw user prompts only and must never be read.

The transcript itself is surprisingly rich and is written live (io.py:1128-1132 opens with mode "a"): a session header with a timestamp ('# aider chat started at 2026-10-21 07:17:16', local time, no TZ), a startup banner carrying the model id ('> Main model: gpt-5 with diff edit format', legacy '> Models: ...'), a repo banner ('> Git repo: .git with 300 files'), per-turn user markers ('#### <prompt>'), and tool lines with the edited file ('> Applied edit to src/main.rs'), shell runs ('> Running <cmd>'), commits ('> Commit <sha> <msg>') and a per-turn token report ('> Tokens: 5,244 sent, 604 received...'). So project, model, current-file basename, normalized tool activity, phase and an elapsed timer are all recoverable — all of them verified against a REAL upstream transcript fixture (Aider-AI/aider tests/fixtures/chat-history.md).

The blocker is location, not format: Discodex's session_sources() only returns roots under dirs::home_dir(), and aider's transcript sits in the root of whatever arbitrary repo the user launched aider in, with no home-level index, no per-project directory and no session id. A drop-in adapter therefore needs new discovery machinery (config-listed repo roots, or enumerating aider.exe processes and reading their CWD from the PEB) plus a main.rs change so a session snapshot can coexist with the existing focused-window fallback (today has_session_tracking() would suppress the working focused "Aider" presence). The line format also has no structured tool records — tool activity must be inferred from English console lines, which is churn-prone (aider already renamed 'Models:' to 'Main model:'), so the parser must be a strict literal allow-list that emits only fixed labels, basenames and model ids.

Verdict: PARTIAL. The data needed for Codex-level richness exists locally and is tailable line-by-line with the existing LogTailer (no zstd, no new crate, no SQLite), but a default install is not discoverable by a home-rooted watcher, the tool/phase signal is string-derived rather than structured, and the file contains full prompts/responses/diffs — so a privacy-strict allow-list parser plus opt-in path discovery is mandatory. Keep the existing focused-app detection for Aider as the fallback; do not flip has_session_tracking() until discovery works.
